title: My Family Trip to Hanoi
source_body:
My Family Trip to Hanoi
Posted by Yuri | August 15, 2026

Last week, my family spent five days in Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam. It was my first trip abroad, and I want to share some of my favorite memories.

The first thing that surprised me was the traffic. There were thousands of motorbikes on the streets, and crossing the road felt like an adventure! Our tour guide told us to walk slowly and steadily so that drivers could see us and go around us.

On the second day, we visited Hoan Kiem Lake in the center of the city. In the evening, the streets around the lake were closed to cars, and local families came out to dance, play games, and enjoy street food.

Speaking of food, I fell in love with Vietnamese cuisine. My favorite was bun cha, grilled pork served with rice noodles and fresh herbs. It cost only about 50,000 dong, which is less than 3,000 won!

The highlight of our trip was a boat tour of Ha Long Bay, which is famous for its thousands of limestone islands. The view was so beautiful that I couldn't stop taking pictures.

If you ever have a chance, I highly recommend visiting Hanoi!

My Family Trip to Hanoi
Posted by Yuri | August 15, 2026

Last week, my family spent five memorable days in Hanoi, the bustling capital of Vietnam. Having never traveled overseas before, I would like to share a few of the experiences that left the deepest impression on me.

What astonished me first was the traffic: thousands of motorbikes flooded the streets, turning every road crossing into an adventure! Our tour guide instructed us to walk slowly and steadily so that drivers could anticipate our movements and steer around us.

On the second day, we visited Hoan Kiem Lake, situated in the very center of the city. In the evening, the surrounding streets were closed to vehicles, and local families poured out to dance, play games, and savor street food.

Speaking of food, I became utterly captivated by Vietnamese cuisine. My personal favorite was bun cha, a dish of grilled pork accompanied by rice noodles and fresh herbs. Remarkably, it cost a mere 50,000 dong, which amounts to less than 3,000 won!

Without a doubt, the highlight of our journey was a boat tour of Ha Long Bay, renowned for its thousands of limestone islands. So breathtaking was the scenery that I could not stop taking photographs.

Should you ever have the opportunity, I would wholeheartedly recommend visiting Hanoi!
